destination.heading: Azorius Senate
destination.philosophy: Azorius trusts law, information, documentation, and procedure to make civic life legible and protected, while recognizing that process must remain accountable to people.
destination.tagline: Law, procedure, and enforceable structure protect civic order when they stay accountable to the people they govern.

destination.heading: White
destination.philosophy: White believes peace is not a mood. It is a structure: rules that hold, shelter that lasts, and obligations people can trust under pressure.
destination.tagline: Safety is built, not assumed.

destination.heading: Blue
destination.philosophy: Blue believes no one is finished by default. Knowledge, practice, and precise systems let people and worlds become more than their starting shape.
destination.tagline: Possibility opens when the pattern is understood.

destination.heading: Black
destination.philosophy: Black believes the world offers no guaranteed fairness. It secures agency by treating life, death, loyalty, and resources as costs that can be paid for control.
destination.tagline: Power is protection when no one is coming to save you.

destination.heading: Red
destination.philosophy: Red believes feeling is a form of truth. Freedom becomes real when the impulse is allowed to move now, before fear, permission, or overthinking can smother it.
destination.tagline: The honest spark moves before the cage closes.

destination.heading: Green
destination.philosophy: Green believes the world is not an unsolved machine. It is a living order already holding each creature's place, and strength comes from accepting nature, rooting deeply, and letting time reveal what was always in the seed.
destination.tagline: The seed remembers what it is becoming.

destination.heading: Boros Legion
destination.philosophy: Boros philosophy joins civic order with urgent protection. Its best expression acts when harm is present, but remains accountable to the public duty it claims to serve.
destination.tagline: Public protection. Disciplined action.

destination.heading: House Dimir
destination.philosophy: Dimir turns information into hidden leverage through secrecy, backroom dealing, observation, and delayed disclosure.
destination.tagline: Secrets, backroom deals, and hidden information leverage.

destination.heading: Golgari Swarm
destination.philosophy: Golgari treats death, decay, and discarded matter as useful material inside a living cycle: undercity survival, food production, graveyard resources, and renewal rather than generic morbidity.
destination.tagline: What is discarded can feed the next cycle.

destination.heading: Gruul Clans
destination.philosophy: The Gruul were assigned Ravnica's wild places, then urban expansion and other guilds eroded that role. Their red-green identity centers loose clans, Rubblebelt territory, direct action, riot and bloodrush pressure, and anger at imposed civilization.
destination.tagline: Wild places lost. The clans answer directly.

destination.heading: Izzet League
destination.philosophy: The Izzet League turns blue-red curiosity into elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, spell engines, and prototypes. Its best work makes discovery useful; its pressure point is volatile experimentation that can outrun care, procedure, or restraint.
destination.tagline: Invent first. Stabilize what the experiment teaches.

destination.heading: Orzhov Syndicate
destination.philosophy: Orzhov is the white-black Ravnican guild where religious legitimacy, deal-making business, debt, and cartel hierarchy overlap. Vox Mana reads it through collectible obligation and institutional leverage, not generic WB attrition, lifegain/drain, taxes, sacrifice, recursion, or removal mechanics alone.
destination.tagline: Debt, deals, and hierarchy made official.

destination.heading: Cult of Rakdos
destination.philosophy: Rakdos turns black-red appetite into public spectacle: performance, provocation, sensation, and visible cost become the way restraint is mocked and hidden pressure is exposed. It is not generic evil or random disruption; the signal is the act, the audience, and the consequence.
destination.tagline: Performance makes appetite, cost, and consequence visible.

destination.heading: Selesnya Conclave
destination.philosophy: Belonging becomes sacred when individual voice joins a greater living community.
destination.tagline: A communal voice rooted in nature and shared purpose.

destination.heading: Simic Combine
destination.philosophy: Simic treats nature as living systems to preserve, heal, study, adapt, and improve through biology, clade practice, and experimentation.
destination.tagline: Life studied as an adaptive, improvable system.

destination.heading: Lorehold College
destination.philosophy: Lorehold treats history as something to recover, question, and put to use. Its scholars pore over artifacts and ancient texts, summon spirits as witnesses, and investigate what surviving records leave behind. White looks for preservation, precedent, and order; Red follows discovery, experience, and messy truths that refuse to stay neatly cataloged.
destination.tagline: Leave no stone unturned.

destination.heading: Jund
destination.philosophy: Jund treats feeling as a compass. Red supplies self-truth and action, Black honors appetite and self-interest, and Green strips away overthinking until instinct can move.
destination.tagline: Trust the feeling. Feed the hunger. Bear the consequence.

destination.heading: Dune / Aggression
destination.philosophy: Dune believes presence should claim ground before detached contemplation can cool the moment. White holds the line, Black authorizes the cost, Red keeps ignition immediate, and Green keeps bodies and pressure multiplying.
destination.tagline: Take the field. Keep the line moving.

destination.heading: Colorless
destination.philosophy: Colorless asks what remains when the five colors are not the grammar of the answer: the artifact that acts without appetite, the void that does not negotiate, the Wastes where colored mana has been stripped away, and the detached perspective that must not become superiority over color.
destination.tagline: Outside the wheel. Not above it.

destination.heading: Five-Color
destination.philosophy: Five-Color gives access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green. It does not establish one unified philosophy by itself; the commander, tribe, mechanic, theme, toolbox, or deck plan determines why all five colors are present.
destination.tagline: All five colors are available. What brings them together depends on the deck.

destination.heading: Azorius Senate
destination.philosophy: In this authored identity, Azorius combines White's standards with Blue's planning and timing. Your recorded answers contributed toward that rule-setting frame; they do not establish personality, skill, or one required deck style.
destination.tagline: Law, procedure, and enforceable structure protect civic order when they stay accountable to the people they govern.
